The nonunit capacity vector satisfies the exact hypothesis of the full-cut exclusion in the same dimension, feasible domain and positive weights. Every strictly positive row therefore has a proper minimum. The pairwise clause assumes proper minima directly and does not require a unit-vector comparison.

A proper threshold lies strictly between vertex heights, so interior points on both sides exist and yield an interior section point on their segment. A relatively open patch inside the simplex gives strictly positive centroid coordinates. The coarea weight for this affine section is constant, so its normalized measure is the normalized section volume used by the gradient fact.

For distinct strictly positive rows and any column, adding s to one and subtracting s from the other is feasible for both signs for small |s|. The derivative is c_i∂_jφ_d(X_i)−c_k∂_jφ_d(X_k) and vanishes. With a single proper row, its positive weighted gradient supplies λ directly.

Integrating the affine identities Σ_j u_j=1 and X_i·u=t_i gives Σ_j(b_i)_j=1 and X_i·b_i=t_i. Summing the components of the common gradient gives S=c_i F_i^(−1/d), and evaluating capacity at the true minimum gives c_iφ_d(X_i)=St_i.

dependencies.application: The matrix dimension, column sums, positive weights, local maximality and nonunit capacity vector match. Its last conclusion supplies properness and uniqueness for every strictly positive row.

An individual strictly positive row at a proper minimum already has the stated capacity gradient and a unique threshold. The fact does not impose cross-row stochastic transfer or multiplier conditions.

The proper-section coarea derivative and actual centroid are already available for a single cut. Neither a capacity-minimizing threshold nor equality of weighted gradients across stochastic rows is part of that fact.
